arxiv-2104-00957.title: A note on some infinite sums of Hurwitz zeta functions
arxiv-2104-00957.creator: R. B. Paris
arxiv-2104-00957.description: Abstract We consider some closed-form evaluations of certain infinite sums involving the Hurwitz zeta function ζ ⁡ ( s , α ) \zeta(s,\alpha) of the form ∑ k = 1 ∞ ( ± 1 ) k ​ k m ​ ζ ​ ( s , k ) , \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}(\pm 1)^{k}k^{m}\zeta(s,k), where m m is a non-negative integer.

arxiv-2108-03314.title: Fulde − - Ferrel − - Larkin − - Ovchinnikov phase in one dimensional Fermi gas with attractive interactions and transverse spin-orbit coupling
arxiv-2108-03314.creator: Monalisa Singh Roy, Manoranjan Kumar
arxiv-2108-03314.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Monalisa Singh Roy, Manoranjan Kumar. We examine the existence and characteristics of the exotic Fulde-Ferrel-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) phase in a one dimensional Fermi gas with attractive Hubbard interactions, in the presence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Zeeman field. We show that a robust FFLO phase can be created in the presence of attractive on-site interactions and Zeeman field, and that the addition of SOC suppresses the FFLO order and enhances the pair formation.

arxiv-2204-02466.title: Aggregating human judgment probabilistic predictions of COVID-19 transmission, burden, and preventative measures
arxiv-2204-02466.creator: Allison Codi, Damon Luk, David Braun, Juan Cambeiro, Tamay Besiroglu, Eva Chen, Luis Enrique Urtubey de Cèsaris, Paolo Bocchini, Thomas McAndrew
arxiv-2204-02466.description: Abstract Abstract: Aggregated human judgment forecasts for COVID-19 targets of public health importance are accurate, often outperforming computational models. Our work shows aggregated human judgment forecasts for infectious agents are timely, accurate, and adaptable, and can be used as tool to aid public health decision making during outbreaks.

arxiv-2204-05214.title: An extended Rayleigh model: Properties, regression and COVID-19 application
arxiv-2204-05214.creator: Gauss M. Cordeiro
arxiv-2204-05214.description: Abstract We define a four-parameter extended Rayleigh distribution, and obtain several mathematical properties including a stochastic representation. We construct a regression from the new distribution. The estimation is done by maximum likelihood. The utility of the new models is proved in two real applications. Keywords : Censored data, generalized Rayleigh; maximum likelihood estimation; regression model, stochastic representation.

arxiv-2204-12830.title: Bound on optimal local discrimination of multipartite quantum states
arxiv-2204-12830.creator: Donghoon Ha, Jeong San Kim
arxiv-2204-12830.description: Abstract We consider the unambiguous discrimination of multipartite quantum states and provide an upper bound for the maximum success probability of optimal local discrimination. We also provide a necessary and sufficient condition to realize the upper bound. We further establish a necessary and sufficient condition for this upper bound to be saturated.

arxiv-2206-05937.title: Data-Driven Denoising of Stationary Accelerometer Signals Journal: Measurements
arxiv-2206-05937.creator: Daniel Engelsman, Itzik Klein
arxiv-2206-05937.description: Abstract Modern navigation solutions are largely dependent on the performances of the standalone inertial sensors, especially at times when no external sources are available. During these outages, the inertial navigation solution is likely to degrade over time due to instrumental noises sources, particularly when using consumer low-cost inertial sensors.

arxiv-2207-04311.title: Lorentz-Violating Electrodynamics in Continuous Matter
arxiv-2207-04311.creator: M.M. Ferreira Jr, P.D.S. Silva, and M. Schreck
arxiv-2207-04311.description: Abstract We review the propagation of electromagnetic waves in continuous matter in the presence of Lorentz-violating terms. First, we briefly discuss classical electrodynamics with regard to optical properties of a dielectric medium exhibiting the Chiral Magnetic Effect. Such a medium can be modeled by Maxwell–Carroll–Field–Jackiw theory.

arxiv-2304-01134.title: On the Impact of Gaslighting on Partially Observed Stochastic Control
arxiv-2304-01134.creator: Shutian Liu and Quanyan Zhu
arxiv-2304-01134.description: Abstract Recent years have witnessed a significant increase in cyber crimes and system failures caused by misinformation. Many of these instances can be classified as gaslighting, which involves manipulating the perceptions of others through the use of information. In this paper, we propose a dynamic game-theoretic framework built on a partially observed stochastic control system to study gaslighting.

I would also like to thank Kevin Purbhoo for discussing his work and clearing any queries I

arxiv-2309-17091.description: Abstract . Our work is motivated by the connection established between Lorentzian polynomials and the Dressian in the seminal work of Brändén and Huh on Lorentzian polynomials. We analyze this relation for the class of positroids, and are able to show that in this case, we can relate a multiaffine homogenous stable polynomial to it.

arxiv-2404-13040.title: Analysis of Classifier-Free Guidance Weight Schedulers
arxiv-2404-13040.creator: Xi Wang, Nicolas Dufour, Nefeli Andreou, Marie-Paule Cani, Victoria Fernández Abrevaya, David Picard, Vicky Kalogeiton
arxiv-2404-13040.description: Abstract Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) enhances the quality and condition adherence of text-to-image diffusion models. It operates by combining the conditional and unconditional predictions using a fixed weight. However, recent works vary the weights throughout the diffusion process, reporting superior results but without providing any rationale or analysis. By conducting comprehensive experiments, this paper provides insights into CFG weight schedulers.

arxiv-2409-16073.title: OW-Rep: Open World Object Detection with Instance Representation Learning
arxiv-2409-16073.creator: Sunoh Lee Minsik Jeon Jihong Min Junwon Seo
arxiv-2409-16073.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sunoh Lee Minsik Jeon Jihong Min Junwon Seo. Open World Object Detection (OWOD) addresses realistic scenarios where unseen object classes emerge, enabling detectors trained on known classes to detect unknown objects and incrementally incorporate the knowledge they provide. While existing OWOD methods primarily focus on detecting unknown objects, they often overlook the rich semantic relationships between detected objects, which are essential for scene understanding and applications in open-world environments (e.g., open-world tracking and novel class discovery).

arxiv-2411-10397.title: Features that Make a Difference: Leveraging Gradients for Improved Dictionary Learning
arxiv-2411-10397.creator: Jeffrey Olmo, Jared Wilson, Max Forsey, Bryce Hepner, Thomas Vin Howe, David Wingate
arxiv-2411-10397.description: Abstract Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are a promising approach for extracting neural network features by learning a sparse and overcomplete decomposition of the network’s internal activations. However, SAEs are traditionally trained considering only activation values and not the effect those activations have on downstream computations.

arxiv-2504-08122.title: Threading the Needle: Test and Evaluation of Early Stage UAS Capabilities to Autonomously Navigate GPS-Denied Environments in the DARPA Fast Lightweight Autonomy (FLA) Program
arxiv-2504-08122.creator: Adam Norton, Holly A. Yanco
arxiv-2504-08122.description: Abstract The DARPA Fast Lightweight Autonomy (FLA) program (2015–2018) served as a significant milestone in the development of UAS, particularly for autonomous navigation through unknown GPS-denied environments. Three performing teams developed UAS using a common hardware platform, focusing their contributions on autonomy algorithms and sensing. Several experiments were conducted that spanned indoor and outdoor environments, increasing in complexity over time.

arxiv-2505-08673.title: A Study of Data-driven Methods for Inventory Optimization
arxiv-2505-08673.creator: Lee Yeung Ping , Patrick Wong , Tan Cheng Han \text{Lee Yeung Ping},\text{Patrick Wong},\text{Tan Cheng Han} † {\dagger}\penalty\ Hong Kong Baptist University ‡ {\ddagger}\penalty\ Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
arxiv-2505-08673.description: Abstract This paper shows a comprehensive analysis of three algorithms (Time Series, Random Forest (RF) and Deep Reinforcement Learning) into three inventory models (the Lost Sales, Dual-Sourcing and Multi-Echelon Inventory Model). These methodologies are applied in the supermarket context. The main purpose is to analyse efficient methods for the data-driven.

arxiv-2507-08297.creator: Zizheng Zhan ∗ † , Ken Deng ∗ , Huaixi Tang ∗ , Wen Xiang ∗ , Kun Wu ∗ , Weihao Li, Wenqiang Zhu, Jingxuan Xu, Lecheng Huang, Zongxian Feng, Shaojie Wang, Shangpeng Yan, Xuxing Chen, Jiaheng Liu, Zhongyuan Peng, Zuchen Gao, Haoyang Huang, Xiaojiang Zhang, Jinghui Wang, Zheng Lin, Mengtong Li, Huimin
arxiv-2507-08297.description: Abstract We present Kwaipilot-AutoThink (KAT), an open-source 40B large language model developed to address the overthinking problem in reasoning-intensive tasks, where an automatic thinking training paradigm is proposed to dynamically switch between reasoning and non-reasoning modes based on task complexity.

arxiv-2508-16532.title: Thermal-orbital evolution of Eris
arxiv-2508-16532.creator: Ryunosuke Akiba, Francis Nimmo
arxiv-2508-16532.description: Abstract The large Kuiper Belt object (KBO) Eris is nearly as big as Pluto and has a small moon, Dysnomia. Constraints on the system’s spin and orbit characteristics were recently used to argue for a dissipative Eris, requiring a differentiated structure but not necessarily a subsurface ocean.

pmc-10613266.creator: Lan-Li Hsueh, Yu-Cheng Yeh, Meng-Ling Lu, Chi-An Luo, Ping-Yeh Chiu, Po-Liang Lai, Chi-Chien Niu
pmc-10613266.description: Over-distraction has been shown to be a risk factor for cage subsidence and postoperative neck pain after anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF). Biomechanical studies have demonstrated increased adjacent segment intradiscal pressure after ACDF. The purpose of this study is to determine if over-distraction of the index disc has an effect on adjacent segment pathology.

pmc-10808718.creator: Apurva Watve, Amelie Haugg, Nada Frei, Yury Koush, David Willinger, Annette Beatrix Bruehl, Philipp Stämpfli, Frank Scharnowski, Ronald Sladky
pmc-10808718.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recent advances in real-time fMRI neurofeedback have successfully demonstrated the modulation of amygdala activity in healthy and psychiatric populations.

pmc-11546611.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Parkinson’s Disease: A Contribution to Cognitive Impairment?
pmc-11546611.creator: Antonella Scorziello, Rossana Sirabella, Maria Josè Sisalli, Michele Tufano, Lucia Giaccio, Elena D’Apolito, Lorenzo Castellano, Lucio Annunziato, Luigi Casella
pmc-11546611.description: Among the non-motor symptoms associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD), cognitive impairment is one of the most common and disabling. It can occur either early or late during the disease, and it is heterogeneous in terms of its clinical manifestations, such as Subjective Cognitive Dysfunction (SCD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and Parkinson’s Disease Dementia (PDD).

pmc-11676778.title: Corticosteroids in Pediatric Septic Shock: A Narrative Review
pmc-11676778.creator: Immacolata Rulli, Angelo Mattia Carcione, Federica D’Amico, Giuseppa Quartarone, Roberto Chimenz, Eloisa Gitto
pmc-11676778.description: Objective: A controversial aspect of pediatric septic shock management is corticosteroid therapy. Current guidelines do not recommend its use in forms responsive to fluids and inotropes but leave the decision to physicians in forms refractory to the first steps of therapy.

pmc-12855673.title: An European consensus on [123I]Ioflupane acquisition and reconstruction using 3D CZT SPECT/CT
pmc-12855673.creator: Diego Cecchin, Alessandra Zorz, Renaud Lhommel, Anthime Flaus, Perrine Tylski, Gregory Mathoux, Neil Hartman, Eric Guedj, Francesca Serani, Laetitia Imbert, Antoine Verger
pmc-12855673.description: IntroductionThe introduction of hybrid SPECT/CT systems with 3D multi-head gantries and CZT crystal detectors offers significant clinical potential, especially for brain imaging. These advancements allow for reduced activity/time requirements, improved spatial resolution, contrast, and the ability to study early perfusion phases and enable 4D acquisitions.

pmc-13136720.title: Femoral diaphysis malunion: An overview
pmc-13136720.creator: Marco Pes, Yahya Ibrahim, Nikhil Pandit, Alexandros Vris
pmc-13136720.description: Femoral diaphyseal fractures are commonly treated with intramedullary nailing; however, malunion remains a clinically significant complication, particularly following delayed presentation, non-operative management, or treatment in resource-limited settings. Femoral diaphyseal malunion may be angular, rotational, longitudinal, or multiplanar and can result in gait disturbance, limb-length discrepancy, patellofemoral overload, secondary joint degeneration, and chronic pain.

pmc-13560024.creator: Shaojie Zhang, Rong Wang, Jingjin Weng, Min Li, Min Shi, Jiazhang Wei, Linsong Ye, Xueying Huang, Wenlin Huang, Shenhong Qu
pmc-13560024.description: BackgroundEpidemiological studies have documented an association between allergic rhinitis (AR) and depression (DE), but causal interpretation is limited by confounding and reverse causation. We applied bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization to assess the direction and magnitude of this association and to explore candidate pathways.

uslaw-usc-t42-s7606.title: 42 U.S.C. § 7606 — Federal procurement
uslaw-usc-t42-s7606.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s7606.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 85 (Air Pollution Prevention And Control); Subchapter III (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Contracts with violators prohibited No Federal agency may enter into any contract with any person who is convicted of any offense under section 7413(c) of this title for the procurement of goods, materials, and services.
